covers.quote: You can use ‘they’ or ‘them’ when you would otherwise use a singular personal pronoun such as:
You can also use ‘themselves’ or ‘themself’ instead of ‘himself’ or ‘herself’.

parts.quote: You must provide copies of the application to your referees.

examples.note: A plural subject avoids specifying gender.

parts.quote: Candidates must provide copies of the application to their referees.
Every candidate must provide copies of the application to referees.

rules.quote: If it’s not clear and you can’t ask them, choose gender-neutral pronouns.
rules.violation_condition: A gender-specific pronoun refers to a person whose pronoun is unclear and who cannot be asked.
when: Applies when the person’s pronoun is unclear and it is not possible to ask them.
Singular ‘they’ and ‘them’ are permitted.
Both ‘themselves’ and ‘themself’ are permitted for a single person.
Rewriting with second-person pronouns, a plural subject or no pronoun is also acceptable.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the unknown-pronoun condition in one check; G-3 treats the permitted neutral forms and rewrites as options, not separate rules.

covers.quote: Avoid using job titles that end in ‘-man’ or ‘-woman’.
Avoid using the traditional terms for jobs that end in ‘-man’.
You should also avoid job terms that specify women.

rules.violation_condition: A gender-specific occupational title is used, including a title ending in ‘-man’, ‘-woman’ or a feminine occupational form such as ‘actress’.
when: Applies to occupational titles, including traditional masculine titles and feminine job terms.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates masculine and feminine occupational forms into the same check; G-4 absorbs the body restatements.

covers.quote: Gender is not relevant to a person’s profession or title in general.
For example, an economic analysis might discuss ‘female-dominated’ or ‘male-dominated’ industries.

rules.quote: Use gender-specific adjectives only when gender is relevant.
rules.violation_condition: A gender-specific adjective is used even though gender is irrelevant to the subject being discussed.
when: Gender-specific adjectives are allowed when gender is relevant.
An economic analysis discussing female-dominated or male-dominated industries is an expressly permitted context.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the relevance condition and its permitted economic-analysis case together; this checks modifiers rather than occupational titles.

rules.quote: Use ‘Mx’ when a person indicates this is what they prefer, but not otherwise.
rules.violation_condition: The title ‘Mx’ is applied to someone who has not indicated that preference, or another personal title is used despite their indicated preference for ‘Mx’.
when: Applies when using a personal title for a person.
Non-binary identity alone does not establish a preference for ‘Mx’.
rules.why: G-2 treats the indicated-preference and no-indicated-preference cases as one conditional title-selection check.

covers.quote: Forms and surveys can ask for people to specify gender.
It does not need to ask for their preferred title.

rules.quote: Don’t ask for a title or gender identity unless the form is designed to collect this information.
rules.specification: Assess whether collection is part of the form’s stated purpose; do not treat the mere presence of a title or gender-identity field as sufficient evidence that the form is designed to collect it.
rules.violation_condition: A form requests a title or gender identity even though collecting that information is outside the form’s purpose.
when: Forms specifically designed to collect the requested title or gender-identity information are excepted.
The guidance also discusses surveys.
rules.why: G-2 keeps title and gender-identity requests under one collection-purpose check; G-3 records the permission without creating a requirement to collect either.

rules.quote: Follow the rule that people have the right to identify their sexual orientation and gender identity as they choose.
rules.violation_condition: A person’s sexual orientation or gender identity is described using an identification inconsistent with the one they have chosen.
when: Applies when referring to a person’s sexual orientation or gender identity and their chosen identification is known.
rules.why: G-4 selects the actionable body sentence rather than the process-oriented heading; the check concerns the identification used in the text.
